newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico long distance phone rates to drop - study.
newsitem.headline: Mexico long distance phone rates to drop - study.

text.p: Mexican long distance telephone rates could drop up to 40 percent in 1997, when services are opened up to competition, a study from the U.S. Trade and Development Agency said.
The study, obtained here Tuesday, said rates will fall by at least 20 percent next year although more "radical" estimates have rates falling by up to 40 percent, the agency said.

But rates are not expected to drop as much as they did in Chile when that South American nation opened up its long distance telephone service to competition. Chilean prices came down by 90 percent, the agency said.
The monopoly of Telefonos de Mexico expires January 1, 1997 and a host of long distance operators are queuing up to provide parallel services.
